/-!
# Erdős Problem 918

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/918](https://www.erdosproblems.com/918)
- [ErHa68b] Erdős, P. and Hajnal, A., On chromatic number of infinite graphs. (1968), 83--98.
- [Er69b] Erdős, P., Problems and results in chromatic graph theory. Proof Techniques in Graph Theory (Proc. Second Ann Arbor Graph Theory Conf., Ann Arbor, Mich., 1968) (1969), 27-35.
-/

universe u

open scoped Cardinal

namespace Erdos918

/-- Is there a graph with $\aleph_2$ vertices and chromatic number $\aleph_2$ such that every
subgraph on $\aleph_1$ vertices has chromatic number $\leq\aleph_0$? -/
-- Formalisation note: source material [ErHa68b] uses only induced subgraphs
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_918.parts.i :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ (V : Type u) (G : SimpleGraph V), #V = ℵ_ 2 ∧ G.chromaticCardinal = ℵ_ 2 ∧
      ∀ (W : Set V) (_ : #W = ℵ₁), (G.induce W).chromaticCardinal ≤ ℵ₀ := by
  sorry

/-- Is there a graph with $\aleph_{\omega+1}$ vertices and chromatic number $\aleph_1$ such that
every subgraph on $\aleph_\omega$ vertices has chromatic number $\leq\aleph_0$? -/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_918.parts.ii :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (ω : Ordinal),
    ∃ (V : Type u) (G : SimpleGraph V), #V = ℵ_ (ω + 1) ∧ G.chromaticCardinal = ℵ₁ ∧
      ∀ (W : Set V) (_ : #W = ℵ_ ω), (G.induce W).chromaticCardinal ≤ ℵ₀ := by
  sorry

/-- Is there a graph with $\aleph_2$ vertices and chromatic number $\aleph_2$ such that every
subgraph on $\aleph_1$ vertices has chromatic number $\leq\aleph_0$? -/
-- Formalisation note: It is not clear whether this question for general subgraphs is open or not
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_918.variants.all_subgraphs.parts.i :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ (V : Type u) (G : SimpleGraph V), #V = ℵ_ 2 ∧ G.chromaticCardinal = ℵ_ 2 ∧
      ∀ (H : G.Subgraph) (_ : #H.verts = ℵ₁), H.coe.chromaticCardinal ≤ ℵ₀ := by
  sorry

/-- Is there a graph with $\aleph_{\omega+1}$ vertices and chromatic number $\aleph_1$ such that
every subgraph on $\aleph_\omega$ vertices has chromatic number $\leq\aleph_0$? -/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_918.variants.all_subgraphs.parts.ii :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (ω : Ordinal),
      ∃ (V : Type u) (G : SimpleGraph V), #V = ℵ_ (ω + 1) ∧ G.chromaticCardinal = ℵ₁ ∧
      ∀ (H : G.Subgraph) (_ : #H.verts = ℵ_ ω), H.coe.chromaticCardinal ≤ ℵ₀ := by
  sorry

/-- A question of Erd\H{o}s and Hajnal [ErHa68b], who proved that for every finite $k$
there is a graph with chromatic number $\aleph_1$ and $\aleph_k$ vertices where each subgraph on
less than $\aleph_k$ vertices has chromatic number $\leq \aleph_0$. -/
-- Formalisation note: the source is missing the assumption that the graph have ℵₖ vertices
-- which can be found in [ErHa68b]
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_918.variants.erdos_hajnal (k : ℕ) (hk : 0 < k) : ∃ (V : Type u) (G : SimpleGraph V),
    #V = ℵ_ k ∧ G.chromaticCardinal = ℵ₁ ∧
      ∀ (W : Set V) (_ : #W < ℵ_ k), (G.induce W).chromaticCardinal ≤ ℵ₀ := by
  sorry

/-- In [ErHa69] the questions are stated with $= \aleph_0$ rather than $\leq\aleph_0$. This is
a likely typo since it can be shown that no such graph exists in this case.

This is the first question with induced subgraphs. -/
@[category textbook, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_918.variants.eq_aleph_0.parts.i :
    ¬∃ (V : Type u) (G : SimpleGraph V), #V = ℵ_ 2 ∧ G.chromaticCardinal = ℵ_ 2 ∧
      ∀ (W : Set V) (_ : #W = ℵ₁), (G.induce W).chromaticCardinal = ℵ₀ := by
  sorry

/-- In [ErHa69] the questions are stated with $= \aleph_0$ rather than $\leq\aleph_0$. This is
a likely typo since it can be shown that no such graph exists in this case.

This is the first question with all subgraphs. -/
@[category textbook, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_918.variants.eq_aleph_0_all_subgraphs.parts.i :
    ¬∃ (V : Type u) (G : SimpleGraph V), #V = ℵ_ 2 ∧ G.chromaticCardinal = ℵ_ 2 ∧
      ∀ (H : G.Subgraph) (_ : #H.verts = ℵ₁), H.coe.chromaticCardinal = ℵ₀ := by
  sorry

/-- In [ErHa69] the questions are stated with $= \aleph_0$ rather than $\leq\aleph_0$. This is
a likely typo since it can be shown that no such graph exists in this case.

This is the second question with induced subgraphs. -/
@[category textbook, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_918.variants.eq_aleph_0.parts.ii (ω : Ordinal) :
    ¬∃ (V : Type u) (G : SimpleGraph V), #V = ℵ_ (ω + 1) ∧ G.chromaticCardinal = ℵ₁ ∧
      ∀ (W : Set V) (_ : #W = ℵ_ ω), (G.induce W).chromaticCardinal = ℵ₀ := by
  sorry

/-- In [ErHa69] the questions are stated with $= \aleph_0$ rather than $\leq\aleph_0$. This is
a likely typo since it can be shown that no such graph exists in this case.

This is the second question with all subgraphs. -/
@[category textbook, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_918.variants.eq_aleph_0_all_subgraphs.parts.ii (ω : Ordinal) :
    ¬∃ (V : Type u) (G : SimpleGraph V), #V = ℵ_ (ω + 1) ∧ G.chromaticCardinal = ℵ₁ ∧
      ∀ (H : G.Subgraph) (_ : #H.verts = ℵ_ ω), H.coe.chromaticCardinal = ℵ₀ := by
  sorry

end Erdos918

findings.description: The binder `∀ (ω : Ordinal)` makes the question ask for a graph at every successor aleph: for every ordinal α, a graph on ℵ_(α+1) with chromatic cardinal ℵ₁ and countably chromatic ℵ_α-sized induced subgraphs. In the source, ω is the fixed first infinite ordinal, not a parameter. Lean's elaborated declaration confirms that this is a genuine universal quantifier. This introduces a substantially stronger, global incompactness question.
findings.source_evidence: https://www.erdosproblems.com/latex/918 asks specifically: “Is there a graph with $\aleph_{\omega+1}$ vertices and chromatic number $\aleph_1$ such that every subgraph on $\aleph_\omega$ vertices has chromatic number $\leq\aleph_0$?” See also Erdős (1969), p. 28, https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1969-13.pdf. The 1968 paper separately discusses possible generalizations to other regular cardinals; they are not quantified in this question.
findings.suggested_fix: Delete `∀ (ω : Ordinal),` and replace both occurrences of the index `ω` by `Ordinal.omega0`. Thus the vertex cardinality is `ℵ_ (Ordinal.omega0 + 1)` and the subgraph cardinality is `ℵ_ Ordinal.omega0`.

findings.description: This repeats the erroneous universal quantification over `ω : Ordinal`. Changing induced subgraphs to arbitrary subgraphs does not justify changing the fixed index ω into every ordinal. The arbitrary-subgraph upper-bound condition is equivalent to the induced-subgraph condition, so it neither repairs nor changes the index defect.
findings.source_evidence: The second question at https://www.erdosproblems.com/latex/918 and in Erdős (1969), p. 28, concerns only ℵ_(ω+1) and ℵ_ω, with ω the first infinite ordinal: https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1969-13.pdf.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the ordinal quantifier and use `Ordinal.omega0` in the two aleph indices, retaining the quantification over `H : G.Subgraph`.

findings.description: The declaration asserts the result with exactly ℵ_k vertices unconditionally. The cited result with that prescribed vertex cardinality assumes GCH. In particular, Corollary 1 of [ErHa68b] begins “Assume G.C.H.”; its ξ = 0 case supplies the stated ℵ_k-sized graphs. The preceding unconditional Theorem 2 instead uses the cardinal exp_(k−1)(γ)^+ and asserts chromatic number greater than γ. The website's unrestricted-size summary does not justify adding `#V = ℵ_ k` while omitting the hypothesis of the sized corollary.
findings.source_evidence: Erdős–Hajnal, On chromatic number of infinite graphs (1968), §3, p. 86, Corollary 1: “Assume G.C.H. Then for every ξ and for every 1 ≤ k < ω there exists a graph ...” with size ω_(ξ+k), chromatic number ω_(ξ+1), and small subgraphs of chromatic number at most ω_ξ. https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1968-04.pdf. Lambie-Hanson–Rinot, §2.1, likewise records the k = 2 Erdős–Hajnal result with the hypothesis `2^{ℵ₀} = ℵ₁`: https://arxiv.org/abs/1708.06929v1.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a GCH hypothesis, for example `hGCH : ∀ α : Ordinal.{u}, (2 : Cardinal.{u}) ^ (ℵ_ α) = ℵ_ (α + 1)`, and document it. Alternatively, if formalizing the unconditional unrestricted-size statement on the problem website, remove the added vertex-cardinality conjunct rather than attributing it to the unconditional result.

findings.description: The parameter `(ω : Ordinal)` again replaces the fixed first infinite ordinal, and here the resulting statement is demonstrably false. At ω = 0, take the complete graph on `(ℵ₁ : Cardinal.{u}).out`. Its size and chromatic cardinal are ℵ₁, and every ℵ₀-sized induced subgraph is complete and has chromatic cardinal ℵ₀. Thus it satisfies exactly the existential predicate being negated. This counterexample and the negation of the universally quantified declaration were proved in `/workspace/review/scratch.lean` without `sorryAx`. The fixed-ω nonexistence statement was also proved there.
findings.source_evidence: The equality version in Erdős (1969), p. 28, asks about a graph of size ℵ_(ω+1), with chromatic number ℵ₁, whose ℵ_ω-sized subgraphs have chromatic number ℵ₀. It does not quantify over ordinal indices. https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1969-13.pdf. The equality/inequality discrepancy is discussed at https://www.erdosproblems.com/latex/918.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove `(ω : Ordinal)` and use `Ordinal.omega0` in both indices. A separately documented generalized lemma could instead assume `0 < α`; that positive-index version is true, but allowing α = 0 is not.

findings.description: The four equality-variant docstrings, at lines 81, 91, 101 and 111, cite `[ErHa69]`, which is absent from the bibliography. The paper printing the equality versions is the sole-authored Erdős 1969 paper listed as `[Er69b]`, not an Erdős–Hajnal 1969 reference.
findings.source_evidence: The module bibliography identifies `[Er69b]` as Erdős, Problems and results in chromatic graph theory (1969), pp. 27–35. The equality questions occur on p. 28 of that paper: https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1969-13.pdf. The website also attributes the equality wording to `[Er69b]`: https://www.erdosproblems.com/latex/918.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace `[ErHa69]` by `[Er69b]` in all four equality-variant docstrings.

status_issues.source_status: Part (i) is settled as an independence result, relative to large-cardinal consistency assumptions: Baumgartner (1984) established consistency with GCH of the required graph, while Foreman–Laver (1988) established consistency with GCH of its nonexistence. The website still marks the combined two-part problem OPEN, but the later literature explicitly records both results for part (i).
status_issues.evidence: Lambie-Hanson–Rinot, Reflection on the coloring and chromatic numbers, §2.1, https://arxiv.org/abs/1708.06929v1: the incompactness list attributes to Baumgartner consistency with GCH of an `(ℵ₀,ℵ₂)`-chromatic graph of size ℵ₂; the compactness list attributes to Foreman–Laver consistency with GCH that no such graph exists. Their definition of `(μ,κ)`-chromatic uses chromatic number κ and chromatic number at most μ on every smaller subgraph, equivalent here to the condition in part (i).
status_issues.suggested_change: Mark this part `research solved` and document its independence, including the relative consistency qualifications. Retain the answer placeholder rather than choosing an unconditional True or False; the repository already supports this convention for independent problems.

status_issues.recorded: research open; answer(sorry), with a comment questioning the status of the all-subgraph version
status_issues.source_status: The same independence result applies to this declaration. Its upper-bound condition is equivalent to the induced-subgraph condition, so there is no separate unresolved all-subgraph case.
status_issues.evidence: Lambie-Hanson–Rinot, §2.1, https://arxiv.org/abs/1708.06929v1, records the positive consistency result of Baumgartner (1984) and the negative consistency result of Foreman–Laver (1988). The equivalence of the two declarations' graph predicates was independently proved in Lean.
status_issues.suggested_change: Use `research solved`, document the same independence result as for part (i), retain an appropriately explained answer placeholder, and remove the comment suggesting a separate uncertainty for general subgraphs.

reformulations.difference: The website says every subgraph, whereas this declaration quantifies only over induced subgraphs. The file also gives an all-subgraph variant and expresses uncertainty about its relation to the induced version.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For any vertex set W, the induced graph G[W] is a subgraph of G. Conversely, every H : G.Subgraph is a spanning edge-subgraph of G[H.verts], so a coloring of G[H.verts] restricts to a coloring of H.coe. Hence the chromatic upper bound for all induced subgraphs of a specified cardinality is equivalent to the bound for all subgraphs of that cardinality. Both the general equivalence and the complete existential statements for part (i) were proved in the scratch file. The same argument applies to the subgraph choice in part (ii), independently of its erroneous ordinal quantifier.

reformulations.difference: This declaration also uses an arbitrary ordinal parameter instead of the source's fixed ω. Unlike the induced equality variant, however, this generalization does not change the truth of the nonexistence claim.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For every ordinal α, ℵ_α ≤ ℵ_(α+1). Any proposed graph therefore has a vertex subset W of size ℵ_α. The subgraph with vertex set W and no edges has chromatic cardinal at most 1, strictly below ℵ₀, contradicting the required equality. This proves the nonexistence claim uniformly for every α, and thus proves its equivalence to the fixed-ω nonexistence claim. `/workspace/review/scratch.lean` contains the explicit equivalence proof, with no `sorryAx` dependency.

sources_consulted: Erdős–Hajnal, On chromatic number of infinite graphs (1968), especially introduction and §3, pp. 83, 86–89: https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1968-04.pdf
Erdős, Problems and results in chromatic graph theory (1969), especially pp. 27–29: https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1969-13.pdf
Lambie-Hanson–Rinot, Reflection on the coloring and chromatic numbers, introduction and §2.1; LaTeX source and abstract: https://arxiv.org/abs/1708.06929v1

Honzik, Compactness for small cardinals in mathematics: principles, consequences, and limitations, subsection on chromatic compactness and transfer principles; LaTeX source and abstract: https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.27618v5
Todorčević, Combinatorial dichotomies in set theory, §§1–2 and 8: https://www.math.toronto.edu/stevo/dichotomies4.pdf
Rényi Institute collected-papers index, used to locate the cited papers: https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/ and https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/Erdos.html
review.notes: All nine declarations were checked. The final `/workspace/review/scratch.lean` compiles successfully and contains independent proofs of chromatic-cardinal attainment, complete-graph and empty-graph boundary cases, the k = 1 witness and k = 0 obstruction, the induced/all-subgraph equivalences, the valid equality nonexistence variants, and the ordinal-zero counterexample. Printed axiom dependencies for these proofs contain no `sorryAx`. The GCH finding concerns the prescribed-size Erdős–Hajnal corollary; the main questions were compared with the unconditional wording on the website and in the 1969 paper. No unconditional polarity is being inferred from the independence results. The reviewed file remains unchanged.

submission.summary: Replaced the erroneous ordinal quantifiers with the fixed constant Ordinal.omega0 in the two part (ii) questions and the induced equality variant. Added the GCH hypothesis to the prescribed-size Erdős–Hajnal theorem and updated its docstring to cite Corollary 1. Also corrected the trivial [ErHa69] citation typos to [Er69b]. Changes are confined to 918.lean; the requested compile command succeeds with only declaration-uses-sorry warnings.
